title: Expressive mobile-first palette and compact scale overhaul
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Update Redwood's design tokens with a mobile-first intent: introduce an expressive but accessible color palette, compress the typography scale for small screens, rationalize spacing/radius steps, and simplify elevation layers for cross-platform parity. This ticket covers token definitions, Figma token file updates, engineering migration notes, and accessibility checks.
acceptance_criteria: New color palette exported as semantic tokens (surface, text, interactive, positive, caution, negative) with WCAG AA contrast for body text at small sizes
Typography scale reduced to an 8-step compact scale with clear mapping from legacy sizes and migration table
Spacing/radius defined as a 6-step modular system with explicit use-cases (stack/gutter/card/padding)
Elevation simplified to four semantic levels with token names usable in CSS/Android/iOS runtimes
Figma file updated and linked; Engineering PR includes automated token migration scripts; design review approved
No visual regressions on core product routes (Console dashboard, API keys page, Model catalog) beyond acceptable thresholds
engineering_notes: Eng review requested: ensure token names follow existing naming conventions or provide a compatibility layer (alias tokens) for 2 releases. Plan for a Node-based migration script to rewrite CSS custom properties and update mobile JSON bundles. Benchmark visual diffs on staging via Percy/Galaxy. Backend config flags available to gate rollout by customer tier.
decisions: Adopt semantic token naming rather than low-level color tokens (e.g., text-primary instead of gray-700) to enable swapping palettes per theme/region
Compact typography: move from 12-step to 8-step scale; map legacy tokens using a migration table in the PR
Spacing: use a 6-step scale (s0..s5) with scale factors of 4px, 8px, 12px, 16px, 20px, 28px to better fit mobile density
Elevation: reduce to surface-0..surface-3 with simplified shadow recipes tuned for mobile compositing performance
Introduce explicit fallback/alias tokens for backward compatibility for at least 2 release cycles
tradeoffs: Reducing the typography steps and spacing granularity simplifies component layouts and reduces token surface area, but may require per-component tweaks to maintain pixel-perfect parity on desktop. Providing aliases increases initial complexity in the token build pipeline but reduces churn for downstream components.
review_comments: PM - Jordan Kim: Please ensure the new palette supports high contrast accessibility mode; highlight colors for charts need to maintain separability at small sizes.
Engineering - Priya Desai: Migration script should include a dry-run mode and a changelog of updated files. Also flag components that use computed tokens (JS-in-CSS) for manual audit.
Design - Lena Sørensen: Reduced radius set looks cohesive on mobile but needs visual QA for data tables on desktop where compactness could harm legibility.
Accessibility - Omar Greene: Confirm contrast ratios at 14px and 12px body sizes with both normal and bold weights; provide test cases in storybook
